sources.entry: Bubo Reader - Irrationally minimal RSS feed reader. (Demo) MIT Nodejs

summary.one_liner: Bubo Reader is a hyper-minimalist, static-page RSS, Atom, and JSON feed reader that builds a single HTML page of links from feeds grouped by category.
summary.what_it_does: Bubo Reader fetches the latest items from a set of feed URLs listed in conf/feeds.json, organized into categories and websites. It renders them through a Nunjucks HTML template into a static public/index.html page with a stylesheet. The build is run with npm scripts (npm run build:bubo), and the output can be served from any static host. The README describes the code as split into src/index.ts (fetch and build), src/renderer.ts (Nunjucks rendering), and src/utilities.ts (parsing and normalization). Request batching is configurable through MAX_CONNECTIONS and DELAY_MS, with the default set to no throttling. The README includes a Netlify deployment path using a netlify.toml file, and suggests external schedulers or a cron job to trigger rebuilds.
use_cases: Self-host a simple page of links from RSS feeds
Read blogs and news feeds without a tracking-heavy reader
Deploy a static feed dashboard to Netlify
Group feeds by category on one webpage
Schedule periodic rebuilds of a feed page with cron
how_to_run: Edit feeds.json (conf/feeds.json) with your categories and feed URLs
Serve the generated static page in the public folder, or deploy to Netlify using netlify.toml
notable: Deliberately minimal: outputs a single static HTML page with no server-side reader app
Feeds are defined in a plain JSON file grouped by category
Template and renderer are swappable (Nunjucks template plus renderer.ts)
Configurable batching and throttling of feed requests via MAX_CONNECTIONS and DELAY_MS
caveats: Rebuilds are needed to pick up new content; the page does not update on its own, so you must set up a scheduled trigger (Netlify build hook with an external service, or cron)
README gives no detail on read state, accounts, or interactive features
